newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London fall sharply on U.S. data, Dow.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London fall sharply on U.S. data, Dow.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London plunged after stronger than expected U.S. payrolls data fuelled fears of U.S. interest rate rises and sent the Dow tumbling.
"The market was a touch easier before the figures, down around 15-points as people cleared their books ahead of the numbers, but now we've collapsed in a heap," said one senior trader.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was 243.34 points or 1.84 percent lower at 12,948.16 by 1446 GMT.
U.S. December non-farm payrolls rose by 262,000 against forecasts of a 192,000 increase.
U.S. bonds sank and the Dow was off 54 points by 1450 GMT as investors fretted over a near-term U.S. interest rate hike.
The initial markdown in London came on the back of a 6.61 point fall on the Hang Seng to 13,191.50 overnight.
Weaker Hong Kong property stocks and sliding Japanese shares had conspired to weigh on sentiment.
Dealers said property stocks continued to be hit in London, especially after the U.S. numbers.
"The property stocks were hit hard," said a London dealer. "The U.S. long bond is indicating higher interest rates which is particularly affecting the sector."
Elsewhere, traders said stocks were marked down similarly across the board. Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings was trading at HK$165.35 in London after a Hong Kong close of HK$168.00.
